title: DeLisa sidemen and the wartime draft
summary: Sonny Cohn, Johnny Board, Harlan Floyd, Cy Touff, Dennis Farnon and Earl Washington played in the band, which had high turnover from the draft; Saunders was 4-F.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, who were some of the musicians in the band when you started, as it went on?
Well, we had so many of them. The boy who at one time, it was about six of my ex-men in Basie's band. Johnny Board was in there.
Sonny Cohn worked in there?
Sonny Cohn worked with me for nine years. We worked down in the Downbeat Room.
Oh, down on Randolph?
Randolph Street. Sonny was with me then. Yeah, right.
I remember that.
Yeah, right.
I came up from Louisville when I was about 16, and walked up and down --
Right, right, Randolph, that was a -- oh, man that was just like Broadway then.
Yeah, Red Allen --
Right. We followed Red Allen in there, right. Yeah. So -- yeah, Sonny Cohn and Harlan Floyd-Booby --
I know Booby, oh, yeah, I've played a lot with Booby.
Well, that was his first thing into the band here.
Cy Tooff worked with you for awhile.
Cy Tooff worked with me for a long time.
That's where he learned how to play.
Right. And then Farnum, Dennis
Farnum.
The writer?
Yeah, the writer, and then -- right, he used to write for me. And he played trumpet for me for a-while.
And he has a brother who writes.
Yeah, Brian. Brian Farnum, yeah, right.

And -- oh, I just had all kinds of guys there, at the Delisa that worked -- these was just a few of them. Earl Washington, he was a former brother-in-law of mine, and I knew him before he could even play. And I gave him his first job.
Really?
Right.
Earl left too soon.
Yeah, right, right, and he --
Nice player.
Nice fellow, nice player.
Yeah, I liked Earl very much.

Yeah, right, right, right. So -- and we had -- during the way, you just had a tremendous turnover in the musicians. Guy would be with you two months or three months, and then he would get his induction papers and that was it.
So I didn't go to the Second World War because they gave me a 4-F.
